svg.title: TOPAK A6 — The lifecycle is secured at its boundaries: every boundary declares what crosses it, its instant, its adversary and its owner, and a boundary with no instant is a finding
svg.desc: ADR-0070 (Proposed, 2026.11.13; revised R1 the same day on an adversarial review) reads the lifecycle in six phases the custodian settled ⟨K1⟩, examines every boundary ⟨K2⟩ and every production target artifact ⟨K3⟩, and puts both halves of the tandem developer in scope ⟨K4⟩. It gives every boundary seven declared things, keeps the register's B1 to B14 under their ids and adds B15 to B29, and applies the corpus's own rule everywhere: a crossing that adds authority has an instant at which a quorum, an issuance or a promotion decides it, and a crossing that subtracts is local. Nothing here is modelled, checked or built: the two modules of §13 are not written, no dependent entry of §11 is drafted, the reference does not recompute the signed digest at load (F1), and seven boundaries have no instant today. The custodian decided none of its content. The placing of boundaries on phases in the picture is this diagram's; the register's own picture is A3 and is not redrawn here.
svg.text: TOPAK · A6

text.tspan: The lifecycle is secured at its boundaries: every boundary declares what crosses it, its instant, its adversary and its owner, and a boundary with no instant is a finding

svg.text: ADR-0070 (Proposed, 2026.11.13; revised R1 the same day on an adversarial review) reads the lifecycle in six phases the custodian settled ⟨K1⟩, examines every boundary ⟨K2⟩ and every production target artifact ⟨K3⟩, and puts both halves of the tandem developer in scope ⟨K4⟩. It gives every boundary seven declared things, keeps the register's B1 to B14 under their ids and adds B15 to B29, and applies the corpus's own rule everywhere: a crossing that adds authority has an instant at

which a quorum, an issuance or a promotion decides it, and a crossing that subtracts is local. Nothing here is modelled, checked or built: the two modules of §13 are not written, no dependent entry of §11 is drafted, the reference does not recompute the signed digest at load (F1), and seven boundaries have no instant today. The custodian decided none of its content. The placing of boundaries on phases in the picture is this diagram's; the register's own picture is A3 and is not redrawn
here.

text.tspan: Proposed · C2, C4 on the drafter's reading · 2026.11.13 · R1 2026.11.13
Proposed · merged to main at bb76b46, which is not ratification
Derived and frozen; superseded by §2 for citation
Run since e1acade; four pass on a crash (F6); four gates not run

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian settled four things, ⟨K1⟩ to ⟨K4⟩, and decided none of the content: every rule is the drafter's, marked *(drafter's choice)* where an alternative was live and *(drafter's recommendation)* where the choice is left open; the boundary, row, assumption and finding ids are the drafter's (provenance note). C2 attaches because §2 and §3 claim to inventory every boundary and every artifact and §10 claims the rows the lifecycle adds: under ADR-0045 an omission is a false claim, not a gap.

C4 attaches because the record would resolve debts accepted records carry (T-0045-30, T-0045-13 with ADR-0069 §6, G11 item 66). C1 and C3 do not attach (Status note). R1 was made on an adversarial review by a second session of the same model, which gives independence of context and not of lineage and is not ADR-0029 A2's reader (provenance note; review annex). G12 §9 item 115 lists what the record still owes: the custodian's decision on disclosing F1, dispositions for F1 to F9, two rows that fail ADR-0045 §2, the two §13
modules, four gates not run, signed tags, owners for tenancy and jurisdiction, §11's entries. One author, one day, one review.

text.tspan: Six phases ⟨K1⟩, and every boundary §2 names placed on the phase whose instant checks it (the placing is this diagram's; the names are §2's)

text.tspan: Phase 1 · The trusted base for standing up Build (§4)
Evaluated before the first round; every row identified before it runs

svg.text: A stand-up declaration precedes the first Build round of any deployment, and of genesis. It instantiates
ADR-0045 Annex A and §10's rows (§4.1).
Nothing third-party runs before its full SHA-256 is checked; a 16-hex prefix is a label, a floating reference is
refused (§4.2). The full-digest check moves the channel from trust root to delegated, and no further: it
fixes which bytes run, not whether their publisher was honest (T-0070-9).
Order: tools by digest; the toolchain's reproducibility check; the floor gates; the specifications and their results;
the mechanism build (§4.7).
Crosses: tools, crates, images, toolchains. Instant: fetch and install.
State: no instant. The install scripts and the OPA and Kafka images check nothing; the TLC jar, cvc5, elan's
installer and the locked crates are checked by full digest (§2.2).
Crosses: the build. Instant: rebuild and compare.
State: "No reproducible build is declared" (T-0045-30; §2.4).
Crosses: issuances. Instant: signature by the key set.
State: dev keys in the clear (G6; §2.2). The key ceremony comes before any key a deployment trusts exists

text.tspan: The build host is a Build principal's host (§4.5)

svg.text: Ephemeral, built from a declared image, appraised as ADR-0034 appraises a guest. A host that outlives its
round is a degeneracy. One stands today: the proofs' evidence is produced on the custodian's own
arm64-darwin machine, under a prover pin upstream no longer serves, and CI cannot rerun it (F8).

text.tspan: Phase 2 · Development is a Build round; the tandem developer ⟨K4⟩ at a gate (§5)
The agent half: a havoc drafter,

svg.text: The assistant is to the corpus what a Thinker is to the mechanism. Nothing it produces takes effect except
through the custodian's act. It cannot be a row of ADR-0045 §2, so it is excluded, as models are (T-0070-1).

text.tspan: The exclusion holds only as far as A-0070-1 does.

svg.text: Crosses: drafts and commits on a branch. Instant: the custodian's merge (§5.1).
State: plan mode, and asks for commit and push; nothing else. .claude/ is writable by the assistant and
measured by no manifest (F7; §2.4).
Crosses: everything the session reads. Instant: none.
State: no instant. A session can read embargoed safety findings and any key in the workspace (A-0070-6;
Crosses: a pass or a refusal. Instant: the required check.
State: a ratcheted check passes on a crash, and every check runs from the change's own tree (F6; §2.4).

text.tspan: The human half is at the gate, and the gate is hardened (§5.2)

svg.text: The custodian is not evictable, so the custodian is at the gate (ADR-0002 A2, B14). Asked for: a
hardware-backed second factor, signed commits and tags, branch protection, the custodian merging locally,
ratification as a signed tag carrying the Batch manifest's SHA-256. At (1, 0) one compromised account is a
compromised corpus, and nothing here removes that.
Crosses: ratification, merge, tag. Instant: the merge or the tag.
State: 104 of 149 commits unsigned at 981bc77, the 45 signed are GitHub's merges; main reported protected,
its rules not read; one code owner (§2.4).

text.tspan: Phase 3 · Promotion to production keeps ADR-0024's quorum (§6)

svg.text: Crosses: one artifact, by digest. Instant: promotion.
State: in force as specification; no promotion pipeline exists, and signing is a script step (ADR-0044; §2.1).
ADR-0024 stands: a unanimous grant quorum, veto seats, author recusal, a vote bound to (artifact digest,
gate-evidence digest, rules epoch). Nothing here lowers it (§6.1).
Crosses: a vote. Instant: the tally.
State: outside every theorem, as the register found (§2.4).

text.tspan: Provenance is a projection; the signature binds the bytes that load; code is reproduced

svg.text: Provenance and the bill of materials are projected from the sealed round, as ADR-0035 projects Persona
lineage: "a gate over manifests checks what the author claims" (§6.2).
The mechanism recomputes the signed digest at load. ADR-0069 §7 S-1 recomputes at signing; the
recomputation at load is what this record adds, and it is where F1 is (§6.3).
Two builders that share no host, account or key build from the same pinned toolchain and produce the
same digest, or the promotion stalls (§6.4). This is the gate ADR-0069 §6 G-4 finds mechanism code lacks.

text.tspan: Reach is staged, in rounds (§6.5) · the temporal row "Promotion reach"

svg.text: A promotion's reach is a field of the tally; it advances ring by ring after a bake-in with no finding. Silence is not
a pass: a round counts only with evidence the ring's Observers and correlator were live. Only rounds the
operator's schedule opens count. A finding may stop the advance, and never cause it (ADR-0007).
Counted in rounds, not time (ADR-0032 §2). Unbuilt (§2.3).
Crosses: reports upstream. Instant: declaration.
State: Proposed (ADR-0058 §6; §2.1). B11, the deployment rung, is unchanged: ADR-0023 and ADR-0058
own it (§2).
Nothing is fetched at runtime except by digest; freshness is the rules epoch, a log position and not a clock.
Retreat is a revocation (local, an operator's, ADR-0031 §5); return is a promotion, because it adds the
earlier artifact's reach back.

text.tspan: Phase 4 · The runtime secures each artifact ⟨K3⟩ for its whole life (§7)
The register's boundaries keep their place on A3 (§2; §7.1)

svg.text: B2 membrane · B3 typed effect · B4 verified / parameterized · B5 facts / payloads · B6 Contained / Mediated
· B7 seat · B8 Persona / provider · B9 retention / erasure · B10 human authority · B12 guest / host / hypervisor
/ hardware · B13 epoch / lease. Each is restated in §2's tables below; A3 places them on the system.
The runtime records stand and are not restated (§7.1): the lease (ADR-0031), attestation at grant
(ADR-0034), fencing without a clock (ADR-0032), decide, order, re-check (ADR-0015 E1), Observer coupling
(ADR-0039), the forensic floor (ADR-0028), break-glass (ADR-0052).
Crosses: consensus messages. Instant: every message.
State: not built (G5: "none (replica TCP)"; §2.2). A precondition before any deployment (§7.6).
Crosses: control actions. Instant: each action, signed.
State: bearer token and socket mode at the reference (G5; §2.2). A precondition before any deployment (§7.6).
Crosses: Actuate. Instant: channel fidelity, P4.
State: the reference reads node configuration (I44, G19; §2.2).
Crosses: —. Instant: —.
State: absent (register §10.7; §2.3). W and L are measured in every deployment that declares a T_irrev,
which gives B26 an instant (§7.7).

text.tspan: Every promoted artifact has a declared end; an advisory becomes a revocation (§7.2,

svg.text: An artifact with no expiry, no revocation path and no retirement event is a finding (§7.2).
When an advisory names a component in a promoted artifact's SBOM, the operator triages it and revokes
the digest when the affected code is reachable: targeted, local, no quorum, no peer (ADR-0031 §5). Each
deployment declares how much one revocation may stop at once; past that bound it is staged (§7.3). The
temporal row "Advisory to revocation": local; unbuilt (§2.3).
Invariant monitors (§7.4, a recommendation): a correlator fold per proved module; its finding may only
subtract (ADR-0051). Key rotation is an issuance; a compromise is a revocation then an issuance (§7.5).
stood up in order (§4.7)
a pull request's merge;
the Batch's signed tag
B1: one artifact by
digest, a quorum's vote

text.tspan: A finding closes only when a check that would have caught it exists (§9)

svg.text: A check that fails on the defect and passes on the fix: a TLC mutation, a planted-defect test, a floor test, a regression case. A finding with no possible check is carried as debt, not closed *(drafter's choice)*. Each finding gets exactly one row in one register,
with a severity, an owner record and the boundary of §2 it is against: the review counts 108 findings "carried by no list" (CR-60).

Drills run as ADR-0052 §6 counts them, in rounds and not in time: break-glass, the advisory-to-revocation path of §7.3, the retreat of §6.7, and a stand-up from nothing (§4) by someone other than the custodian. A new boundary that no row names is a C2
finding against this record (Re-read).

text.tspan: Phase 5 · Run reaches Build in three ways, and no other (§8)

svg.text: Crosses: Run's records, traces and outcomes. Instant: intake, a promotion of a corpus-root revision (§8).
State: no instant on this tree. ADR-0069 gives it one (IG-1 to IG-7), Proposed. ADR-0047 §9 leaves Build's Read unlabelled (§2.1).
Adversary: TM1 shaping its own output; TM13; poisoning. Owner: ADR-0069 §3 to §5 (Proposed); this record for the removal form (§8).
A Build-domain Observer or correlator finding is ground for Vote(deny) at a
veto seat (ADR-0038 §6, ADR-0051 §3), or for a revocation. This is in force
today (§8.1).
Recorded traces enter the specification graph's runtime layer (ADR-0057 §1,
Proposed) at the grade of their edge. Evidence about a module and never a
premise of an admit (§8.2).
By ADR-0069's intake (§3 to §5). A corpus-root revision is promoted under
ADR-0024. A source: run object is computed from the log and never written;
generatedBy is projected (RR-1). Payloads and labelled items are admitted only
once Build labels, and erasure follows the data (LR-1 to LR-3) (§8.3).

text.tspan: Nothing Run originates enables a Build act (§8)

svg.text: ADR-0069 §2 says so; this record gives it ADR-0065 §1's form: for every Build admit and every promotion, the same request with every Run-originated item removed must still be permitted. Run intake may inform what a person drafts. It never satisfies a
gate, fills a vote, or stands in for evidence.

Through the drafter ⟨R1⟩: Run's output reaches the assistant as untrusted ingress and a draft from that session carries no Run provenance, so a session that has read Run-derived material marks its drafts, and the removal test counts a marked draft as
Run-originated (§5.1, §8). Keeping such material out of drafting sessions altogether is stricter and left open.

The adversary is TM1, writing its own future training data. ADR-0069 §4 makes that influence "visible and attributable" and "Nothing in them makes it harmless". An evaluation suite built from intake is a Build artifact with its own lineage record (ADR-0035), and
it may only refute.
Run's records, traces and outcomes
a deny: Vote(deny) at a veto seat, or
a revocation (§8.1)
Act: an erratum, an amendment, an
R-revision, a new record, a new
release (§9)
Detect (§9)

text.tspan: Every boundary declares seven things, and a boundary with no instant is a finding (§1) ⟨K2⟩

svg.text: The register's columns (items 1 to 5)
What may cross, typed.
The register's columns
Its instant: the event at which the crossing is checked. ⟨R1⟩ An instant names the
predicate checked there, and the evidence that shows the check ran. An event with no
predicate is not an instant.
The register's columns
Its interval of untruth: how long the boundary's claim may be false.
The register's columns

text.tspan: What happens if the check cannot run.

svg.text: The register's columns
Its adversary: who is assumed to attack it, named against TM1 to TM14 (ADR-0068)
where one fits. ⟨R1⟩ That includes an adversary to what crosses being read, not only to
its being changed.
The two its assessment found missing *(drafter's choice)*
Its owner: the record that decides it.
The two its assessment found missing *(drafter's choice)*

A crossing that adds authority, reach or trust has an instant at which a quorum, an issuance or a promotion decides it. A crossing that subtracts is local, needs no quorum, and may run on a local monotonic clock (ADR-0032
A boundary with no instant is not a control. It is a finding, entered in §12 or the review's register, and carried until an instant exists.

The register (§6) calls it the orientation of every boundary: "crossing toward more authority requires consensus, crossing toward less is local and monotone". This record applies the corpus's own design (havoc principals, typed
crossings, digests, quorums for additions, local subtraction) to the parts of the lifecycle that do not yet have it. It invents no new kind of mechanism (Context).

text.tspan: The record's relation to the register (A3)

svg.text: The register's B1 to B14 keep their ids. B15 onward are new (§2). "State" says what exists at e1acade ⟨R1⟩.
The register is derived and frozen. It is superseded by §2 for citation and stays as it is (§11).

The register's own assessment named the two columns it lacked, "Weak: no per-boundary adversary, no owner column" (ToO §10); they are items 6 and 7. Its §10 named eight categories "absent entirely"; records since closed parts of several (ADR-0032, ADR-0034, ADR-0031 A2). Four are still absent:
the toolchain and supply chain (§10.3), tenancy (§10.4), jurisdiction (§10.5) and measurement (§10.7) (Context).

This diagram's reading of that list against §2: tenancy is B24, jurisdiction B25 and measurement B26, each marked "Absent (register §10.n)" in its State cell; the toolchain and supply chain is B18, which the record owns itself and whose State cell cites §4.2 and not the register.

This diagram's count: all fourteen register boundaries appear. B1 to B7 in §2.1; B12 in §2.2; B8, B9, B10, B13 in §2.3; B14 in §2.4; B11 by the note under §2.4, unchanged and owned by ADR-0023 and ADR-0058.

Owed on ratification: ToO §10 and §13, the boundary inventory beside the register, and A-0070-1 to 6 (§11). The temporal axis keeps the register's organizing correction: temporal is an axis that crosses every boundary, and ADR-0032 decides which intervals may use which clock (§2.3).

text.tspan: The boundary inventory, every row (§2) ⟨K2⟩ · Instant cells name the event; the predicate and its evidence are owed per row (Open obligations)

text.tspan: B11, the deployment rung, is unchanged (§2)

svg.text: ADR-0023 and ADR-0058 own it. It is the one register boundary with no row in §2's tables.
The predicate and its evidence for each row, when a deployment instantiates §2 (§1 item 3). Confidentiality across the inventory: R1 names one boundary (B29) and one
assumption (A-0070-6), for the drafting session only. Tenancy (B24) and jurisdiction (B25), each still without an owner record.

text.tspan: Context: the corpus secures the admit path, and the lifecycle around it in pieces; ADR-0069 and this record divide the ground
The tree shows the same gaps (Context, at

svg.text: ⟨R1⟩ At 981bc77 there was no CI, and the review found four checkers that "pass, or stay silent, on a failure" (CR-57). At e1acade, ADR-0069 §10.2's workflows run on every pull request. Four of their seven checks run through a ratchet that passes a checker which
crashes (F6).

⟨R1⟩ The install scripts check no digest when they download (tools/install-tla.sh line 15, tools/install-tlaps.sh line 36, curl -L). The TLC jar is tracked and checked against a full digest (tools/TLA-PIN, tools/check-pins.sh). CI checks cvc5 and
elan's installer by full digest. Cargo checks the SHA-256 that mechanism/Cargo.lock records for 435 of its 443 packages; the other eight are the workspace's own.
tools/TLAPS-PIN says "The release tag floats". The pin is a 16-hex prefix, and "The full digest is owed".

⟨R1⟩ mechanism/docker-compose.yml (line 9) runs openpolicyagent/opa:latest. mechanism/scripts/build-bundle.sh (line 22) compiles the bundle's Wasm with the untagged openpolicyagent/opa, which no Annex A row names.
manifests/EXCLUDE keeps the install scripts and the pin-enforcing wrappers (tools/tlapm, tools/tlc) out of every checkpoint manifest. ⟨R1⟩ It keeps .claude/ and .github/ out too (F7).

⟨R1⟩ 104 of the 149 commits on the branch carry no signature. The 45 that do are merges GitHub made. GitHub reports main as protected. Its rules were not read. CODEOWNERS names one owner for every path.
T-0045-30 reads: "No reproducible build is declared".

"Every record, specification, proof, policy, test and line of code was written or ratified by one person, working with an AI assistant" (REVIEWERS_GUIDE). ToO §0: "Assisted drafting is now the rule and not the exception". ADR-0029 has no criterion for it (G11 item 66).

The assistant's constraints are three lines of .claude/settings.json: NotebookEdit denied, git commit and git push asked, and plan mode by default. The rest is skill prose. The review's highest finding: "the corpus can now be extended faster than it can be
kept true" (CR-61).
Where both speak, this record defers to ADR-0069 (Context; the table whole)
ADR-0069 decides it; this record cites it
ADR-0069 repurposes f1-tla's workflows; this record asks fail-closed checkers of them. ⟨R1⟩ They conflict: §10.2's ratchet passes a checker that crashes, and §5.3 refuses that (F6)
S-1 recomputes the digest at signing; this record adds a recomputation at load (F1)
G-4 finds mechanism code has no gate; this record proposes one
ADR-0069 decides them; this record adds the removal form of "enables nothing" and the evidence path
They differ. §10 reconciles them on one condition

ADR-0069 decides one ordered path from intake to rollout: its stages, intake into a corpus root, return from Run, gates as programs with signed evidence, signing after the tally, and carriers. This record decides what every boundary declares, the inventory, each

artifact's life after rollout, the tandem developer, the stand-up, staged reach, the advisory path and the improvement loop. Companion: ADR-0069 (Proposed, merged to main at bb76b46 ⟨R1⟩). Its §11, §12, Options, Annexes and History were not read (provenance
note).
register; ToO §10 and §13. Closes nothing.

text.tspan: Every production target artifact has a build-side check, a boundary check, run checks and an end (§3) ⟨K3⟩
Proposed · the common rule is the drafter's choice

svg.text: The artifacts are the kinds the records name as crossing B1 (ADR-0024 §1 and A3; ADR-0035 §4; ADR-0054, Proposed), plus the two that reach Run without promotion (the genesis bundle and anchor issuances). The common rule, for every row:
Built in a Build round from pinned inputs, by allowlisted tools only (ADR-0022 §3), so its sealed
topic-set digest is its provenance (ADR-0021 §4).
The digest that is signed and voted on is the digest of the bytes the mechanism will load. Not a source
digest, a revision string or a file name. The load recomputes it (F1). ⟨R1⟩ Where more than one
engine evaluates the artifact, as the bundle's sidecar and its in-process fallback do, each is held to the
signed digest.
An SBOM the gate projects from the round's consumed set as ADR-0035 §1 projects lineage. An
authored SBOM is a cross-check, and a divergence is *Contested*.
⟨R1⟩ By a second, independent builder from the same pinned toolchain, and the digests must match
Expiry, revocation or retirement.

text.tspan: Phase 1 (§4) and Phase 2 (§5), item by item
§4 · The trusted base is evaluated before the first round ⟨K1⟩

svg.text: 1. A stand-up declaration precedes the first Build round of any deployment, and of genesis *(drafter's choice)*. For each row it records how the row's identity was fixed, and how
that was checked on the host where it runs.
2. Nothing third-party runs before its full SHA-256 is checked: tools, toolchains, crates, container images and Lean and Lake dependencies. The design argument: before the
check, the download channel is a trust root; after it, a substitution can only be refused. ⟨R1⟩ And no further: trust on first use pins an upstream compromise faithfully; crates run
code at build time (build.rs, procedural macros). The publishers stay a trust-root row (T-0070-9).
3. Every platform that runs a pinned tool has its own pin. The Lean pin is arm64-darwin only (ADR-0053); a run on another platform under that pin is unpinned.
4. What enforces a pin is measured: the install scripts and wrappers leave manifests/EXCLUDE (F2), ⟨R1⟩ and so do .claude/ and .github/ (F7). A tool that measures the
corpus, or that a gate runs, is measured with it *(drafter's choice; declaring each as a trusted-base row is open)*.
5. The build host is a Build principal's host: ephemeral, from a declared image, appraised as a guest. ⟨R1⟩ One degeneracy stands today: the proofs' host (F8).
6. The key ceremony comes before any key a deployment trusts exists (ADR-0025). Dev keys never cross into a deployment (G6). Anchor, bundle, verifier, identity-provider and
gate-runner keys are hardware-held, each with a custody row *(drafter's recommendation)*.
7. Order of stand-up *(drafter's choice)*: tools by digest; the toolchain's reproducibility check; the floor gates; the specifications and their results; the mechanism build. Each step
rests only on the ones before it.
8. At genesis, all of this is declared and not yet independently checked. It is T-0045-11's identity, and the full-corpus review of ADR-0029 A2 is where it is first read by another.
§5.1 · The assistant is held to Build's alphabet (the table whole)
The repository and the sources the session
names
Everything read from outside the corpus root is untrusted ingress: web pages, issue and PR text, tool
output, files from elsewhere. An instruction found there is content, not a request (ADR-0048 §3's rule). ⟨R1⟩
Run-derived material marks the session, and §8's removal test counts the draft as Run-originated
Write in a worktree or a session branch
No write to the default branch. No credential that could make one
Allowlisted tools only
The harness's permission list is a tracked, gated artifact; a change to it is reviewed as a change to a floor. ⟨R1⟩
Not yet measured: manifests/EXCLUDE keeps .claude/ out (F7). Egress through a declared allowlist.
Credentials injected by the proxy, scoped to one repository and one branch; ⟨R1⟩ whether a session's
credential could push a tag or another branch was not checked (A-0070-2). No secret in the workspace
A session record
Every commit carries the session link (already the case). The session record names the model that served it,
outside the corpus
Propose a branch or pull request
The custodian's merge is the Vote. The assistant never votes, never ratifies, and is never the reader that
satisfies ADR-0029 A2

text.tspan: Further rules for the agent half (§5.1)

svg.text: A claim the assistant marks Met is a claim, not evidence. Every Met carries the command and digest that make it checkable; the custodian, or CI (§5.3), re-runs it before
ratification.
One session drafts. A different reader reviews. A second session of the same model is independence of context and not of lineage; it does not count as A2's reader unless
the custodian rules that it does.
⟨R1⟩ The exclusion holds only as far as A-0070-1 does. The custodian's merge has no predicate, and admits any file at any length; CR-61 is the evidence that reading falls
behind. Where A-0070-1 does not hold, the assistant and the custodian together are T-0045-11's identity.
⟨R1⟩ What a merge reads is bounded *(drafter's recommendation)*: a pull request touches one record, or one artifact and its tests; every Met is re-run by CI.
⟨R1⟩ The assistant does not grade itself *(drafter's choice)*: a change to a checker, to .claude/, to .github/ or to manifests/EXCLUDE is drafted alone and gated by the
base's copy (§5.3).

text.tspan: §5.2 · The human half is at the gate, and the gate is hardened

svg.text: Account and keys. A hardware-backed second factor on the repository host; commits and tags signed with a hardware-held key; the allowed-signers file tracked. ⟨R1⟩ A
signature is checked against the signers file of the tagged commit's parent, so adding a signer is itself signed by one already allowed.
Branch protection on the default branch. No direct push, no force-push, merge only through a pull request whose required checks have passed. ⟨R1⟩ GitHub reports main as
protected; which rules it holds was not read.
⟨R1⟩ The custodian merges, not the host. A merge made in GitHub's interface is signed with GitHub's key. A ratifying merge is made and signed locally and then pushed, or it
is not a ratification.
Ratification is a tagged act. A Batch is a signed tag over the merge commit; the tag, not the merge, is the instant. ⟨R1⟩ Its message carries the SHA-256 of the Batch's
manifest (ADR-0033). A tag signs a commit id, which is SHA-1 and locates the tree rather than identifying it (ADR-0069 §9 C-5).
The custodian's own environment is declared: part of T-0045-11's identity.
The residual. At (1, 0), one compromised account is a compromised corpus. The bootstrap's custody (ADR-0029, at least five humans) is what removes it, and nothing here
does. ⟨R1⟩ A signature does not stop the host from withholding the newest tag, or serving an older one that is validly signed (§10).

text.tspan: §5.3 · Gates before release run on every change and fail closed

svg.text: The gates *(drafter's choice; the alternative, gates run by hand at each Batch, is today's practice and CR-57's finding)*: tools/check-refs.py, the record lint,
tools/verify-manifest.sh --all, the drift test, spec/proof-sync.sh, tools/lean-sync.sh; the floor gates and cargo test; a dependency audit and a review of each
new crate or version; secret scanning; SBOM generation and a reproducibility check (§6).
⟨R1⟩ ADR-0069 §10.2's workflows run the pins, proof-sync, verify-manifest, drift, lean-sync, check-refs, the record lint, TLC's results, cargo test, the Lean builds and the floor
gates. Four are ratcheted. They run no dependency audit, no secret scan, no SBOM and no reproducibility check.
Each checker fails closed. A checker that passes on an empty input, or skips silently, is a defect (CR-57); each carries a planted-defect test that must fail. ⟨R1⟩ A non-zero
exit, or output without the checker's own closing line, is a refusal whether or not the check is ratcheted; tools/ratchet.py ignores the exit status (F6). A gate runs the base's
copy of its checker *(drafter's choice)*.
Gate evidence is signed by the gate runner under a key issued under ADR-0025 §1 (f): the condition on which T-0045-13 stops being excluded. Until then, evidence is an
operator's assertion. ADR-0069 §6 G-1 and G-2 decide this.
Pace is bounded by review *(drafter's recommendation)*: while a checkpoint is owed, or more than an agreed number of records stand Proposed and unread by anyone but
their drafter, new drafting waits. The review's first remedy for CR-61, written as a stall. The custodian's choice, and the number is open.

text.tspan: Phase 6, the loop, every row (§9) · the trusted base gains ten rows and moves two (§10)
Proposed · ADR-0045 Annex A rows owed

svg.text: Observer and correlator findings; dependency advisories; scenarios and simulations; dated reviews; SECURITY.md reports; upstream reports (ADR-0058 §6); a checker's failure
The finding is recorded
A finding may only subtract wherever it acts at runtime (ADR-0007)
Each finding gets exactly one row in one register, with a severity, an owner record and the boundary of §2 it is against
The row exists
The review counts 108 findings "carried by no list" (CR-60). A finding without a row is lost
If the finding is against something running: a revocation or an epoch fence, at once
The revocation is ordered
Subtraction needs no quorum and waits for none (§7.3)
Applied, declined with reasons, or carried as named debt (ADR-0029 A2's three)
The disposition is written
Silence is not a disposition
The typed act its status allows: an erratum, an amendment, an R-revision, a new record, a new release
A Batch, or a promotion
Accepted text changes only by History row
A check that fails on the defect and passes on the fix: a TLC mutation, a planted-defect test, a floor test, a regression case
The check is in CI
A finding closes only when such a check exists *(drafter's choice)*. A finding with no possible check is carried as debt, not closed
Pins, manifests and the checkpoint
The cut is signed
Each record names the rows of §2 it touches, and each checkpoint re-reads the inventory
The checkpoint
A new boundary that no row names is a C2 finding against this record
§10's rows, whole. Each row is read against ADR-0045 §2: its failure can only subtract, or its identity is issued. Ids are the drafter's
The drafting assistant: model, harness and provider
A wrong or hostile draft, which the custodian's act must catch
None. Nothing it produces is in force without the act (§5.1)
The repository host's access control: branch protection and the custodian's account
Trust root while a merge is the ratification. Delegated once §5.2's signed
An unratified change on the default branch; once delegated, a refusal
Not issued: fails §2 as a trust root (finding F4). Folds into T-0045-11 at genesis
Trust root
A forged ratification
Allowed-signers file, tracked. Not issued until an anchor key set exists

As T-0070-5; or a stall

⟨R1⟩ The pinned toolchain's digest, and a host, account and key the first builder does not share

LR-1)

A label leak into Build
Promotion
Upstream publishers: crate authors, image publishers, tool releasers
Trust root
Anything the published bytes do, at build or at run
The tracked full digests, which fix the bytes and not the publisher. It passes §2 only on the reading T-0070-5 takes, that a pinned digest is an identity
What the gate runner installs untracked: the runner image, the downloads of setup-java and setup-python, apt
packages
Trust root for a gate's verdict, beside T-0045-13
A false pass
T-0045-13, the gate runner, moves from excluded to trust root when its key is issued (§5.3), as ADR-0045 §6 already provides.
T-0045-30 keeps its class. Its residual narrows from "no reproducible build" to ⟨R1⟩ the independence of the two builders and of the double-compiling (§6.4).

text.tspan: Models stay out of the trusted base, including the one that drafts the corpus.

svg.text: ADR-0069 recommends that no carrier be a trust root (C-1, C-2). This record agrees on one condition: if the ratification's instant is a signed tag that a checker verifies against
tracked signers (§5.2), the host can only refuse ⟨R1⟩ *what the tag says*, and it is delegated *for that*. If the merge itself is the act, as today, the host can add, and it is a trust
root that fails ADR-0045 §2.

text.tspan: For integrity, and not for freshness ⟨R1⟩ (§10)

svg.text: The host still serves the bytes every verifier reads. It can withhold the newest tag, or serve an older one that is validly signed, and by §6.7 a return adds reach back. So a signed
tag leaves the host a trust root for which tag is newest, until a verifier holds the latest Batch's manifest digest from somewhere the host does not serve *(drafter's
recommendation)*. Signing the tag is necessary for ADR-0069 §9's recommendation, and not sufficient.

text.tspan: Assumptions of use, beside ToO §13 (§10), whole

svg.text: The custodian reads what is ratified, re-runs every Met before ratifying, and does not delegate the act to the assistant
T-0070-1's exclusion is false: the assistant's output is in force unread, and every claim it drafted is the assistant's
No credential that can write the default branch or a tag is reachable from an assistant session
B20 has no instant
Third-party bytes run only after a full-digest check
T-0070-4 is a trust root, and every "checked", "proved" and "built" rests on the network
⟨R1⟩ The two builders share no host, account or key, and the toolchain's double-compiling uses a compiler of another lineage
§6.4 reproduces a compromise both builders share faithfully
Run intake is admitted only through ADR-0069's intake (§8)
Build reads unlabelled Run output; lineage under-approximates its generators
Nothing embargoed under SECURITY.md, and no key a deployment trusts, can be read from an assistant session
The provider and its logs hold them, and B29 has no instant

text.tspan: Findings F1 to F9 (§12): reported, none fixed here
Open · each to a disposition; F1 under SECURITY.md
F1 · The bundle signature binds a source digest and not the bytes that load

svg.text: build-bundle.sh computes the revision as a SHA-256 over the Rego sources and data.json, compiles the Wasm with the untagged openpolicyagent/opa, and signs
{"revision": R}. topak-bundle reads R from the tarball's own .manifest, verifies the signature over bundle_body(R), and loads data.json and policy.wasm without
recomputing anything against R. A tarball whose .manifest names a signed revision loads whatever Wasm and data.json it carries.
⟨R1⟩ A substituted data.json adds reach: it sets each hosted tool's channel target, the label delivery table, each tool's input types, the tool list and the break-glass Run entries. The
sidecar is held to less: it runs with no verification key. No promoted set is checked at load. The repository is public; whether F1 stays here is the custodian's decision under
SECURITY.md.

text.tspan: F2 · What enforces the tool pins is not measured

svg.text: manifests/EXCLUDE excludes tools/install-*.sh, tools/tlapm and tools/tlc, the scripts and wrappers that fetch the tools and refuse an unpinned one.
At 981bc77 every gate in §5.3 is run by hand. At this tree the drift pins fail on ADR-0054 and ADR-0055, whose bytes have moved since they were pinned, and nothing ran to say so.
⟨R1⟩ Since bb76b46 the workflows run on main; the two drift pins are standing findings that the ratchet lists and passes (ADR-0069 ⟨R3⟩). Visible, and still not fixed.

text.tspan: F4 · The gate's own boundary fails ADR-0045 §2

svg.text: The repository host's access control (T-0070-2) can add, and its identity is issued by nothing. ⟨R1⟩ 104 of 149 commits are unsigned at 981bc77; the 45 signed were made by GitHub,
with GitHub's key and not the custodian's. At genesis this is inside T-0045-11's declaration; after bootstrap it needs an issued key (T-0070-3) or it is not a row.

text.tspan: F5 · Nothing in Annex A names the bundle compiler

svg.text: T-0070-5. T-0045-6 covers OPA at evaluation and not at compilation.

text.tspan: F6 · A ratcheted check passes when its checker crashes ⟨R1⟩

svg.text: tools/ratchet.py ignores the command's exit status and counts only matching output lines; run on a checker that exits with a traceback, it reported "added 0" and exited 0. Four
checks in .github/workflows/checks.yml run through it: the corpus pins, tools/lean-sync.sh, tools/check-refs.py and the record lint. Every step runs the pull request's own
tree, so a change that edits a checker is graded by the edited one. Against ADR-0069 §10.2 (Proposed), and §5.3 here.

text.tspan: F7 · The tools that measure the corpus are not measured ⟨R1⟩

svg.text: manifests/EXCLUDE keeps .claude/ and .github/ out of every manifest: .claude/settings.json, the skills that direct ratification and manifest cutting, the record lint CI runs, the
manifest-cutting script, and the workflows. The assistant can write all of .claude/. F2 named only the install scripts and wrappers.

text.tspan: F8 · The proofs' evidence comes from a host §4.5 would refuse ⟨R1⟩

svg.text: TLAPS runs on the custodian's arm64-darwin machine under tools/TLAPS-PIN, whose release upstream no longer serves, and CI cannot rerun it (ADR-0069 §10.2, G-3). Declared
as a degeneracy at §4.5.

text.tspan: F9 · ADR-0069's Status note and §10.2 say its workflows are not on

svg.text: They have been since bb76b46. Reported and not changed here: it is ADR-0069's to revise (§11).

text.tspan: Dependent entries owed (§11), the ratification condition item by item (§13), and the options

svg.text: §11 · Owed, not drafted here: each a pending entry drafted as its own act, after the custodian's reading
§10's rows in Annex A, and T-0045-13's and T-0045-30's cells. The same amendment owes T-0045-6's stale Annex B cell, which still reads "Bundle
unsigned"
§2's signed body becomes the digest of the loaded bytes and not the source revision (F1), and §3's load recomputes it. Drafted with ADR-0069's entry
on the same record
Computed provenance (§6.2), a second builder (§6.4), and reach as a tally field (§6.5). Touches the bootstrap set, as ADR-0024 A4 does
A criterion for assisted drafting (G11 item 66), from §5.1
The assistant's Submit and the harness permission list as an allowlist (§5.1)
Nothing from this record. ADR-0069 owes ADR-0035 its R-revision, and its §5 LR-1 waits on the record that decides whether Build labels
Since it is Proposed. §10.2's ratchet refuses on a checker's non-zero exit, and gates run the base's checkers (F6). Its Status note and §10.2's "Not yet"
are stale since bb76b46 (F9)
The boundary inventory beside the register, and A-0070-1 to 6 ⟨R1⟩
Derived and frozen. Superseded by §2 for citation and stays as it is
§13 · Ratification condition, item by item
ADR-0069 is ratified first, or with this record, for §8 and the parts of §5.3 and §6 that cite it. A clause here that cites an ADR-0069 clause later withdrawn is withdrawn with it
Not met: ADR-0069 is Proposed. ⟨R1⟩ It is merged to main, which is not ratification

The custodian's reading of every drafter's choice and recommendation: §1 items 6 and 7; §3's common rule; §4.1, §4.6, §4.7; §5.1's exclusion; §5.2; §5.3 including the pace bound; §6.2, §6.4, §6.5; §7.4; §8's three ways; §9's closing rule; §11's listing. ⟨R1⟩ And R1's: §4.4;
§5.1's three added rules; §5.3's base-copy rule; §6.4 as rewritten; §6.5's live-monitor and round rules; §7.3's triage and bound; §8's marking; §10's freshness recommendation

text.tspan: Each row of §10 is read against ADR-0045 §2

svg.text: Not met. T-0070-2 and T-0070-3 fail it as they stand (F4). ⟨R1⟩ T-0070-10 fails it too, and T-0070-9
passes only on the reading T-0070-5 takes
The inventory of §2 is read for completeness by someone other than the drafter, since C2 attaches

A module states the two properties this record adds and its mutations break them, by ADR-0046's method: *staged reach* (no ring is reached before its predecessor's bake-in has passed without a finding, and a finding never advances reach); *intake never enables*
(ADR-0065 §1's removal property, at the Run → Build boundary)
Not met: no module is written

The reference (ADR-0033): the bundle load recomputes the signed digest from the loaded bytes (F1); ⟨R1⟩ the sidecar's bundle is held to the same signature, or its decision does not count (F1); every image used is pinned by digest; every install script checks a full digest
before execution
Not met: nothing is built

text.tspan: CI runs §5.3's gates on every pull request, each with a planted-defect test that fails

svg.text: Not met. ⟨R1⟩ CI runs on this branch since e1acade. Four of its checks pass on a crash and every
check runs the change's own checker (F6). None carries a planted-defect test, and four of §5.3's
gates are not run

text.tspan: The default branch is protected and commits and tags are signed

svg.text: Not met for signing (F4). ⟨R1⟩ GitHub reports main as protected. Its rules were not read, so
protection is not shown to be what §5.2 asks
⟨R1⟩ The custodian decides F1's disclosure under SECURITY.md
§11's dependent entries are drafted, or this record is narrowed so that it owes fewer
A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2)
Not met. ⟨R1⟩ The adversarial review of 2026.11.13 was a second session of the same model, and
is not this reader (§5.1)

text.tspan: A record per phase, six records

svg.text: Not taken for the draft *(drafter's recommendation, left open)*. The six phases share one rule, §1's orientation, and one inventory. Splitting after the custodian's reading is recommended if §5 and §8 are to be ratified before §6's staging, which needs a module

Not taken *(drafter's recommendation, left open)*. ADR-0069 decides one path and its stages; this record decides what every boundary declares, each artifact's life, the tandem developer and the loop, none a pipeline stage. Folding or splitting is the custodian's choice

text.tspan: Adopt SLSA, SSDF or in-toto wholesale

svg.text: Not taken. Each is a practice this record cites and maps to. ADR-0021 rejected an in-toto attestation chain in favour of the sealed topic set. The external levels are a vocabulary for the deployment declaration

text.tspan: The assistant as a trust-root row

svg.text: Rejected. It fails ADR-0045 §2: its failure adds and its identity is not issued. Excluding it puts the weight on the custodian's act (A-0070-1)

text.tspan: The assistant as a seated principal under a lease

svg.text: Not taken now. It would need an issued identity and a mechanism around the harness: the right end state once the corpus has an anchor, left open

text.tspan: Gates run by hand at each Batch, as today

svg.text: Rejected. CR-57 and F3 are what it produces
Rejected. An advance adds reach, and ADR-0032 §2 requires trusted time for such an interval, which the corpus refuses (ADR-0045 §6). Rounds are counted, as ADR-0052 counts drills
Not taken. Incidents, traces and outcomes are how §9's loop learns. They enter as untrusted, labelled, erasable ingress that enables nothing

text.tspan: Signing the source revision, as ADR-0044 §2 does

svg.text: Not kept. It signs a name for the bytes and not the bytes (F1)

text.tspan: ⟨R1⟩ A second builder on a second toolchain, as first drafted

svg.text: Withdrawn. Two toolchains do not produce the same bytes, so the rule could not be met (§6.4)

text.tspan: ⟨R1⟩ A ratchet that passes a checker's crash, as ADR-0069 §10.2 builds it

svg.text: Not kept here. A crash that passes is CR-57's defect inside the gate (F6). A ratchet that refuses on a non-zero exit keeps what ADR-0069 wanted from it

text.tspan: ⟨R1⟩ Keeping Run-derived material out of drafting sessions

svg.text: Left open *(drafter's recommendation: marking, §8)*. Stricter, and it would keep the assistant from the incidents §9's loop learns from

text.tspan: ⟨R1⟩ Revoking on every advisory, as first drafted

svg.text: Revised (§7.3). It made the advisory feed a switch that could stop a fleet

text.tspan: as trusted-base rows instead of measuring them

svg.text: Left open. Measuring is cheaper, and a row would still need an identity, which a manifest gives
One inventory, seven columns, and every hole visible. B18, B19, B22, B24, B25, B26 and B29 ⟨R1⟩ have no instant today, and the table says so in one place.
The tandem developer is placed on the pattern's own terms. A-0070-1 and A-0070-2 can be checked. ⟨R1⟩ The exclusion is only as good as A-0070-1, and §5.1 now says
so.
A full-digest check moves the download channel from trust root to delegated. ⟨R1⟩ It reduces the channel, and not the publishers behind it (T-0070-9).
Every subtracting response needs no quorum and no clock. Every adding one (promotion, a ring's advance, a return, intake) has an instant.
Findings close on a check, which addresses CR-60 at the point where findings are lost.
The trusted base grows by ten rows ⟨R1⟩, three of which fail ADR-0045 §2 as they stand.
⟨R1⟩ A gate runs its checker from the base, so a fix to a checker counts one change after it is written.
Promotion gets slower: a second builder, a staged reach, and computed provenance, which needs ADR-0035's method in force.
Everything in §5.2 is still one person. At (1, 0) a hardened gate is still a single gate.
The record is wide. It cites more than thirty records and owes entries in five records and the ToO, some jointly with ADR-0069: the CR-61 pattern this record also criticizes,
and why §5.3 recommends a pace bound and the Options a split.
One author, one day, and no deployment. ⟨R1⟩ One adversarial review, by a second session of the same model.
The custodian's reading of the drafter's choices, and whether to split (Options).
The two modules of §13.
F1 to F9 ⟨R1⟩, each to a disposition. F1 under SECURITY.md's handling.
Branch protection on the default branch, checked and recorded. ⟨R1⟩ Reported protected; its rules still to be read.
⟨R1⟩ The predicate and its evidence for each row of §2 (§1 item 3).
⟨R1⟩ Confidentiality across the inventory. R1 names B29 and A-0070-6, for the drafting session only.
The assistant as a seated principal once an anchor exists: an issued identity, a lease over a session, and a Persona for the model that serves it.
Tenancy (B24) and jurisdiction (B25), each still without an owner record.
A threshold for §5.3's pace bound, if adopted.
Run-side intake for an overlay (ADR-0059 to ADR-0068, Proposed): a plane's reports to its peers are not Run → Build intake, and this record does not decide them.

text.tspan: The review of 2026.11.13, and where each finding landed (annex, whole) ⟨R1⟩ · History

svg.text: The review is not reproduced elsewhere, as the custodian directed: this table and the ⟨R1⟩ marks are its record. The ordering and severities are the review's; the dispositions are the drafter's, and the custodian has read none of them (annex).

F1 understated: data.json sets where effects go and how labels are delivered; policy.wasm is unsigned; the sidecar's bytes are checked against nothing; no promoted set at load; F1 stated in a public record
Applied. Disclosure left to the custodian
The merged CI's ratchet passes a crashing checker, and every check runs the change's own checker
Applied
The record described 981bc77, not main: no-CI and no-digest claims overstated, a commit count off by one, branch protection checkable
Applied
Context, §2, §12 F3, F4, F9
The custodian's merge has no predicate, so the exclusion rests on A-0070-1, which CR-61 contradicts
Applied
§5.1, Consequences
The tools that measure the corpus are excluded from its manifests and writable by the assistant
Applied
Run's output reaches Build through an assistant session, with no Run provenance on the draft
Applied
A signed tag leaves the host able to withhold or roll back; a tag signs a SHA-1 commit id; the signers file authorizes itself; GitHub signs its own merges
Applied
The second builder on a second toolchain could not be met, and no second Rego-to-Wasm compiler exists
Applied
Staged reach advances on silence, and rounds can be generated by principals
Applied
Revoking on every advisory makes the feed a switch that can stop a fleet
Applied, bounded to §7.3's own trigger
§7.3, Options
A full digest fixes identity and not trust; publishers and runner installs are unlisted
Applied
B18, §4.2, §10 T-0070-9 and T-0070-10, Consequences
Confidentiality is absent from the inventory
Medium
Applied in part: the drafting session only
§1 item 6, B29, A-0070-6, Open obligations
The proofs' evidence comes from an unappraised, unreproducible host
Medium
Applied, as a declared degeneracy
An instant names an event but not the predicate checked, nor evidence that it ran
Medium
Applied to §1; owed for each row
§1 item 3, §2, Open obligations
"A finding closes only on a check" invites checks written to close findings
Medium
Not applied. §9 already carries a finding with no possible check as debt, and §5.3's base-copy rule keeps a check from being written to pass the
change it grades. Whether a check would catch the defect is left to the reader of each closure
The assistant drafted the rules that contain it, from delegated summaries
Medium
Recorded. The review is not A2's reader
CI's path-citation check refused four citations, each a path with a line number joined to it
Applied: each now gives the line in words
Context
History, whole

Initial draft. A seven-column boundary contract; an inventory of twenty-seven numbered boundaries, B15 to B27 new, and three temporal ones; a build, boundary, run and end check for each of fourteen artifact kinds; the six phases ⟨K1⟩; the assistant as an excluded havoc drafter and the custodian at the gate ⟨K4⟩; Run → Build as a deny, evidence

or labelled ingress; a finding closed only by a check; eight trusted-base rows and five assumptions; five findings. Drafted as ADR-0069 and renumbered ADR-0070 before it was committed, at the custodian's direction, since ADR-0069 is in flight on its own branch; deferring to ADR-0069 where the two overlap
The custodian's request of 2026.11.13 ⟨K1⟩ to ⟨K4⟩ and direction on the number; the register; the review;
Revision before ratification

Revised on an adversarial review, after main was merged. Four path citations given with the line in words. The Context, §2's State cells, F3 and F4 brought to e1acade. F1 assessed: a substituted data.json redirects effects and lifts delivery modes, the sidecar is held to nothing signed, no promoted set is checked at load; disclosure left to the

custodian. New F6 to F9. New B28 and B29, and boundaries composing at the assistant. §1: an instant names its predicate and evidence, and an adversary may be to confidentiality. §3 (b), (d); §4.2's limit; §4.4 and §4.5 extended; §5.1 gains three rules and marks Run-derived sessions; §5.2 signs the manifest digest in the tag, checks signers

against the parent, and has the custodian merge locally; §5.3 refuses on a non-zero exit and runs the base's checkers; §6.4 rewritten; §6.5 counts only live, operator-opened rounds; §7.3 triages and bounds; §8 closes the path through the drafter; §10 adds T-0070-9 and T-0070-10, qualifies T-0070-2 for freshness, and adds A-0070-6. §11 owes
ADR-0069 an R-revision. §13, Options, Consequences and Open obligations follow. The review annex maps each finding to where it landed. The title and the decision's orientation are unchanged
An adversarial review of 2026.11.13 by a second assistant session at the custodian's request (the review annex);
the merge of main at e1acade; CI's path-citation check on the merged branch; the custodian's direction to fix the
citations, revise on the findings, and note the process in this record
Drafted 2026.11.13 by the assistant at the custodian's
direction, not reviewed
